caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:ofc-3
attempts.entry_title: Reward-related HFA encoding in human OFC (Saez et al. 2018)
attempts.summary: The patients' choice behaviour held up in this data, as did the finding that orbitofrontal high-frequency activity carries the previous round's choices and outcomes but not earlier rounds. The electrode counts behind the encoding results did not: far more electrodes encoded current choice and outcome variables than reported (risk 84 against 50), most likely because the paper does not fully describe its selection rule. The overlap of signal types within electrodes did not match either. Past-trial signals outlasted current ones but were shorter than reported, and several results depend on how the deposited activity was baseline-corrected. The anatomical findings and the comparisons with healthy participants and broadband power could not be tested, as those data are not deposited.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Saez, Lin, Stolk, Chang, Parvizi, Schalk, Knight and Hsu (2018) on CRCNS ofc-3, which holds orbitofrontal high-frequency activity epochs and behaviour of 10 epilepsy patients playing a gambling task. It tests the behaviour, the regression of HFA on choice, outcome and past-trial regressors, the timing and duration of encoding, the stepwise and mixed-effects checks and the overlap of electrode sets. The broadband signal, the electrode locations and the healthy participants' data are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Saez et al. (2018) from CRCNS ofc-3

outcomes.statement: Of 210 OFC electrodes recorded in 10 patients, 192 were artifact-free and included; each patient played 200 rounds, and timeouts, 9.98% of all trials, were excluded.
outcomes.source: STAR Methods, ECoG Recording, and Behavioral task; Table S2, last row
outcomes.quote: Out of 210 OFC electrodes, 192 were artifact-free and included in subsequent analyses
outcomes.notes: The data set holds 10 patients. It holds 199 electrode columns; seven in s03 (52 to 58) are exact copies of electrodes 45 to 51 in both the 1-kHz and the window arrays, and without them the per-patient counts are 5, 6, 52, 5, 61, 7, 11, 10, 19 and 16, those of Table S2, 192 in all. One of these, s03 electrode 42, holds no data of its own (its 1-kHz trace copies electrode 34 and its windows copy electrode 41), so 191 unique recordings are analysed. Timeouts are 99 of 1,938 rounds, 5.11% (4.95% of 2,000), outside 9.98 plus or minus 0.998, and s10 has 138 rounds, not 200. The share of rounds that have no HFA trial (timeouts and other exclusions), 185 of 1,938 or 9.55%, would fall inside the tolerance; it is shown as a variant, as the claims file defines the percentage on timeout trials. The HFA trials are matched to rounds in order; matching them in reverse gives the same rounds except one s02 trial, where only the forward match agrees with the authors' t-1 values, so the match is unique and no matched round is a timeout.
deviations: The electrode count of 192 is the deposited count with the seven copied electrodes of s03 removed; the analysis itself uses 191, counting each recording once.

outcomes.statement: Patients were approximately risk neutral, choosing the gamble only slightly more often than a risk-neutral baseline model, on 55.9% (plus or minus 8.5%) of trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Economic Choice Behavior in Neurosurgical Patients, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: we found that subjects were approximately risk neutral, choosing to gamble only slightly more often than a risk neutral baseline model (55.9% ± 8.5% of risky choices)
outcomes.notes: The gamble was chosen on 54.9% of non-timeout rounds averaged over patients (SD 8.6, reading (a)) and 55.1% pooled (reading (b)), both within 55.9 plus or minus 8.5. Per patient the share runs from 46.8 to 73.5%. A risk-neutral chooser (gamble when win probability times prize exceeds $10, ties split) would gamble on 53.0%, so patients gamble slightly more often, as the statement says.

outcomes.statement: The proportion of risky choices increased with win probability, well captured by a logit model (p < 0.001, random effects logit analysis).
outcomes.source: Results, Economic Choice Behavior in Neurosurgical Patients, paragraph 4; Figure 1C
outcomes.quote: The proportion of risky choices increased as the offer value (win probability) increased, which was well captured by a logit model of decision under risk (p < 0.001; random effects logit analysis; Figure 1C)
outcomes.notes: Random-effects logit of gamble choice on win probability over 1,839 non-timeout rounds. Slope 4.79 (SE 0.24, p = 1.5e-86) with a random intercept, 5.75 (SE 0.33, p = 6.0e-70) with a random intercept and slope. The share of gamble choices rises from 15 to 17% at win probabilities 0 to 0.1 to 76 to 82% at 0.6 to 1. Per patient the slope is significant and positive in 8 of 10; s04 and s10 show no significant effect.
deviations: The random-effects logit is fitted by maximum likelihood with Gauss-Hermite quadrature (20 points, or 12 by 12 with a random slope) in the helper, with Wald tests from a numerical Hessian; the paper used R and does not name the routine. A standard choice.

outcomes.statement: Patients' choices were sensitive to the expected value of the gamble (prize times win probability), with gamble choices more frequent at higher gamble expected value.
outcomes.source: Figure S2A legend
outcomes.quote: Patients' choices were sensitive to the expected value of the gamble (i.e., the gamble prize times the win probability), with gamble choices more prevalent for higher gamble expected value
outcomes.notes: Gamble choices rise from 16.9% at an expected value of $0 to 68 to 87% above $15. The logit slope on expected value is 0.163 per $ (p = 2e-69) with a random intercept and 0.161 (p = 4e-45) with a random slope as well.

outcomes.statement: The patients' choices were comparable to those of 10 healthy comparison participants (all p > 0.2).
outcomes.source: Figure 1C legend; Results, Economic Choice Behavior in Neurosurgical Patients, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Subjects' choices were significantly affected by likelihood of winning the gamble ... and were comparable to those of healthy participants (gray line; all p > 0.2)
outcomes.notes: The data set holds only the 10 patients. The 10 healthy participants' choices are not in it (data.zip and ofc_behav_data.zip list files for s01 to s10 only), and the paper names no other deposit.

outcomes.statement: Reaction times were longer in high-conflict trials (win probability 40 to 60%) than in low-conflict trials (below 30% or above 70%), in patients and in healthy subjects (both p < 0.001, t test), with comparable effect sizes.
outcomes.source: Figure S2B legend
outcomes.quote: Patients and healthy subjects took longer to react in high-conflict trials (both p<0.001, t-test), and the effect size was comparable between both groups

statistics.about: healthy subjects, high against low conflict

outcomes.notes: RT is buttonpress.time minus choice.time (game presentation). High-conflict RTs are longer on average (1.691 against 1.476 s over pooled trials, Cohen's d 0.07; 179 ms per patient, d_z 0.57), but p = 0.165 for the pooled two-sample test (reading (a)) and p = 0.104 for the paired test over 10 patients (reading (b)), neither below 0.001. s10's reaction times are not bounded by the 2-s limit (median 4.4 s, up to 80.5 s) and dominate the pooled test; without s10 the pooled test gives p = 2.2e-06 and the paired test p = 0.147 (variant). Per patient the difference runs from -200 to 932 ms. The healthy subjects' part and the comparison of effect sizes cannot be tested (no data). Leaving s10 out is not a reading the claims file allows; it is shown for sensitivity only.
deviations: Game presentation is taken as the csv column choice.time, which the data description does not list; it is 0.66 to 0.97 s after trial start, near the paper's 750 ms.
RT is taken as buttonpress.time minus choice.time, an inference from the data; the description does not define these columns.

outcomes.statement: Past and current regressors were nearly uncorrelated (mean R2 2.1%, maximum R2 3.7%).
outcomes.source: Results, Dissociable OFC Encoding of Past Choice and Outcome Information, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: past and current regressors were uncorrelated (mean R2 = 2.1%; max R2 = 3.7%)
outcomes.notes: The regressors are the authors' own (sXX_behav_globals.mat) over the HFA trials, with t-2 to t-5 built by the same convention. Mean and maximum R2, averaged over patients and on pooled trials, are (a) own t-1 pairs 0.37 and 0.70% averaged, 0.25 and 0.64% pooled; (b) all current by t-1 pairs 0.53 and 1.73%, 0.23 and 1.20%; (c) all current by t-1 to t-5 pairs 0.59 and 2.29%, 0.21 and 1.71%. None is within 2.1 plus or minus 0.21% and 3.7 plus or minus 0.37%. Past and current regressors are uncorrelated, more so than the paper reports. Over the 1,839 non-timeout rounds the criterion names (variant, regressors built from the rounds), the mean R2 is 0.21 to 0.56% and the maximum 0.64 to 1.87% across readings, also outside the tolerance.

outcomes.statement: Regressors were weakly correlated between and within categories (mean R2 0.15, all R2 below 0.6).
outcomes.source: Figure S6A legend
outcomes.quote: Regressors were weakly correlated between and within categories (mean R2=0.15, all R2<0.6)
outcomes.notes: For the 8 current regressors (reading (a)), the mean R2 over 28 pairs is 0.155 on pooled trials and 0.165 averaged over patients, both within 0.15 plus or minus 0.015; the largest pair is loss index with RPE (0.55 pooled, 0.57 averaged), below 0.6. With the 8 t-1 regressors added (reading (b), 120 pairs) the mean is 0.072 pooled and 0.079 averaged.

outcomes.statement: OFC HFA encodes the choice regressors (risk, gamble choice, offer value, chosen value), time locked to game presentation, and the outcome regressors (gamble win, gamble loss, RPE, regret), time locked to outcome reveal, with average %EV above chance and a rise in the number of encoding electrodes.
outcomes.source: Results, OFC HFA Reflects Choice- and Outcome-Related Valuation Signals, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 3A to 3D; Table S2
outcomes.quote: we found robust evidence within the HFA band for multiple valuation components related to choice (risk, gamble choice, offer value, and expected value of chosen option ... and outcome (gamble win, gamble loss, RPE, and regret) processing
outcomes.notes: Encoding electrodes (p < 0.05 in 5 or more consecutive windows of either epoch) over 191 electrodes are 84 risk, 71 gamble, 61 offer value, 41 chosen value, 59 win, 54 loss, 52 RPE and 64 regret, none within 10% of Table S2 (50, 34, 31, 26, 45, 33, 28, 35). The 95th percentile of the shuffled counts is 48 to 50; chosen value (41) does not exceed it, the other seven do. The timing holds; the mean %EV of the choice regressors peaks 750 ms after game presentation, that of the outcome regressors 800 ms after time 0 of the buttonpress epoch (250 ms after a reveal at +550 ms, the claims file's timing), and the per-window share of electrodes at p < 0.05 peaks at 850 ms for both under reading (b) (850 and 650 ms under reading (a)). The selection classifies 18.2% of electrodes as encoding under shuffled labels, on average about 35, more than Table S2 reports for chosen value, which suggests the paper's selection differs in a detail it does not state (finding). A variant that also requires an electrode's longest run to exceed the 95th percentile of its own shuffled runs gives 41, 31, 21, 12, 24, 15, 15 and 17, all below Table S2. Per patient most encoding electrodes are in s03 and s05, as in Table S2. Under the claims file's baseline readings (a) and (b) the counts are 75, 82, 54, 51, 74, 51, 64, 63 and 66, 74, 56, 37, 68, 41, 50, 45, none within 10%, and chosen value stays below the 95th percentile of its shuffles (51 against 55, 37 against 47), so the outcome is the same under all three.
deviations: The HFA is used as deposited, as the authors' own baseline correction (an assumption): the game epoch is corrected over [-1000, -800] ms (its first window is the same in every trial) and the buttonpress epoch carries a per-trial offset close to it. STAR Methods say only that epochs were made "using a 200-ms baseline to remove any pre-stimulus differences in baseline amplitude", and the data description that "activity for both epochs is temporally aligned". The claims file's readings, (a) the 200 ms before each epoch's event and (b) the 200 ms before game presentation for both epochs (the buttonpress epoch first put on the game epoch's level with its per-trial, per-electrode offset, measured where the epochs overlap), are applied on top of it in the notebook's section Baseline readings.
The analysis uses 191 electrodes (the paper 192); s03 electrode 42 holds no data of its own.

The buttonpress epoch's time 0 is read as the outcome reveal, as the data indicate; the claims file's timing (reveal 550 ms after time 0) is shown alongside, and the timing condition holds under both.

outcomes.statement: The delays of choice encoding after game presentation and of outcome encoding after outcome reveal did not differ (512.5 plus or minus 59 ms against 287 plus or minus 114.33 ms, p = 0.14, t test), nor did their transient durations (612.15 plus or minus 132.9 ms against 712.5 plus or minus 112.5 ms, p = 0.58).
outcomes.source: Results, OFC HFA Reflects Choice- and Outcome-Related Valuation Signals, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: The delays after the presentation of external information, game presentation and outcome reveal, respectively, were not statistically different (512.5 ± 59 ms and 287 ± 114.33 ms; p = 0.14; t test), with transient activation profiles of comparable duration (612.15 ± 132.9 ms and 712.5 ± 112.5 ms, respectively; p = 0.58; t test)
outcomes.notes: With the outcome reveal at time 0 of the buttonpress epoch, the choice and outcome delays do not differ under reading (a) (peak of the mean %EV, 800 plus or minus 74 against 650 plus or minus 87 ms, p = 0.235) or reading (b) (first window above the shuffled share, 512.5 plus or minus 101 against 325 plus or minus 132 ms, p = 0.301), and the durations do not differ (687.5 plus or minus 155 against 1,000 plus or minus 158 ms, p = 0.207). Under reading (b) both delays are within the paper's values, the choice duration is within 612.15 plus or minus 132.9 ms and the outcome duration is not. With the reveal 550 ms after time 0 (the claims file's description of the epoch) the delays differ (p < 0.001 under (a), 0.006 under (b)). Under the per-electrode reading (c), less supported by the claims file, the delays differ (p = 0.026) and the durations do not (p = 0.462). Under the claims file's baseline readings (a) and (b), reading (a) of the delays gives p = 0.224 and 0.200 and the durations p = 0.118 and 1.000; reading (b) of the delays gives p = 0.034 under baseline (a) and 0.052 under baseline (b). The outcome holds under all three baselines, as reading (a) holds under each and one reading suffices.
deviations: The outcome rests on the reading of the buttonpress epoch as locked to the outcome reveal. The data description says the epoch is centred on the button press; the data show it is centred 470 to 600 ms after the csv's button press and that the gamble outcome is encoded from about 200 ms after its time 0, which fits a reveal-locked epoch, and the paper's Figure 3C labels the epoch "time locked to gamble outcome (t = 0)". The true event times are not in the files.

Delay and duration are measured on windows that start at or after the event; the chance profile is the mean %EV of the electrodes selected under the 1,000 shuffles, and the chance share for reading (b) the 95th percentile of the shuffled share per window. Standard choices, as the paper does not define them.
The HFA is used as deposited; the claims file's baseline readings, shown in the notebook, give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Across all regressors the proportion of encoding electrodes was greater with HFA than with broadband field potentials (mean 20.9% against 3.3%, p < 10^-5, t test), and greater in every instance.
outcomes.source: Results, OFC HFA Reflects Choice- and Outcome-Related Valuation Signals, paragraph 4; Figure S4A
outcomes.quote: Across all regressors, the proportion of encoding electrodes identified using HFA was significantly greater than using FP (mean HFA = 20.9% versus FP = 3.3%

statistics.n: not stated; read as 16 regressors (8 current, 8 t-1)

outcomes.notes: The data set holds only HFA (game_events_hg, buttonpress_events_hg and their window averages); there is no broadband field potential or raw voltage, and the paper names no other deposit. The HFA side alone gives a mean proportion of encoding electrodes over the 16 current and t-1 regressors of 33.3% (from the tables of fig3-present-encoding and fig4-past-encoding), against the paper's 20.9%. Under the claims file's baseline readings it is 31.1 and 25.8%, also outside 20.9 plus or minus 2.09.

outcomes.statement: Broadband power modulation across OFC was maximal at the button press and weak at the time of maximal HFA outcome encoding (about 750 ms after outcome reveal), so HFA encoding is distinct in time from broadband modulation.
outcomes.source: Results, OFC HFA Reflects Choice- and Outcome-Related Valuation Signals, paragraph 4; Figure S4B
outcomes.quote: ERP modulation is maximal at the time of button press, and thus does not align in time with maximal encoding of outcome information
outcomes.notes: No broadband signal is in the data set. The HFA side can be measured; the mean %EV of the outcome regressors peaks 800 ms after time 0 of the buttonpress epoch, which the data indicate is the outcome reveal (within 750 plus or minus 75 ms), or 250 ms after a reveal at +550 ms. Under the claims file's baseline readings it peaks at 700 and 800 ms.

outcomes.statement: HFA encodes characteristics of the preceding trial; past choice and outcome features are widely represented across OFC except past risk, dissociable from current signals.
outcomes.source: Results, Dissociable OFC Encoding of Past Choice and Outcome Information, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 4A to 4D; Table S2
outcomes.quote: features were widely represented across the OFC, with the exception of past risk, and were dissociable from current choice and outcome signals
outcomes.notes: Encoding electrodes for the t-1 regressors are 40 risk, 64 gamble, 59 win probability, 53 chosen value, 67 win, 79 loss, 76 RPE and 95 regret. The seven other than risk exceed the 95th percentile of their shuffles (48 to 50) and past risk has the lowest count, below its 95th percentile (49). None of the eight counts is within 10% of Table S2 (17, 43, 46, 35, 49, 56, 50, 64). The mean %EV of the t-1 regressors is above chance in 56 of 57 game-epoch windows and all 57 buttonpress-epoch windows. The own-null variant of fig3-present-encoding gives 9, 33, 27, 22, 35, 37, 28 and 40. Under the claims file's baseline readings (a) and (b), only 2 and 1 of the seven past regressors other than risk exceed their shuffles, and under (b) past risk is not the lowest, so the outcome rests on the deposited baseline (assumed).
deviations: The HFA is used as deposited, as the authors' own baseline correction (an assumption): the game epoch is corrected over [-1000, -800] ms (its first window is the same in every trial) and the buttonpress epoch carries a per-trial offset close to it. STAR Methods say only that epochs were made "using a 200-ms baseline to remove any pre-stimulus differences in baseline amplitude", and the data description that "activity for both epochs is temporally aligned". The claims file's readings, (a) the 200 ms before each epoch's event and (b) the 200 ms before game presentation for both epochs (the buttonpress epoch first put on the game epoch's level with its per-trial, per-electrode offset, measured where the epochs overlap), are applied on top of it in the notebook's section Baseline readings.
The t-1 regressors are the authors' file values, which keep rounds after a timeout with 0 for the choice and outcome regressors. The analysis uses 191 electrodes.

outcomes.statement: Past-trial signals were sustained; the longest continuous stretch of significant encoding was longer for past outcome (1,341.37 plus or minus 49.63 ms) and past choice (1,169.15 plus or minus 61.2 ms) than for current choice (799.6 plus or minus 36.94 ms) and current outcome (706.9 plus or minus 30.56 ms), all p < 10^-6, t test.
outcomes.source: Results, Dissociable OFC Encoding of Past Choice and Outcome Information, paragraph 2; Figure 5A and 5B
outcomes.quote: both past outcome (average duration = 1,341.37 ± 49.63 ms) and past choice (1,169.15 ± 61.2 ms) showed significantly more sustained activation than current choice and outcome signals (799.6 ± 36.94 and 706.9 ± 30.56 ms, respectively; all

statistics.about: each past group against each current group
statistics.n: electrode and regressor pairs with encoding, per group

outcomes.notes: Under epoch reading (a) and stretch reading (a), mean durations are 669.9 (past outcome, n = 317), 650.7 (past choice, 216), 534.2 (choice, 257) and 462.0 ms (outcome, 229); adding the 150 ms of the window (readings (b) and (c), which coincide) gives 819.9, 800.7, 684.2 and 612.0 ms. Both past groups are longer than both current groups with p from 8.0e-07 to 8.8e-03, all below 0.01, but only past outcome against current outcome is below 10^-6. Under epoch reading (b) past choice against current choice gives p = 0.011. No mean is within the stated SEM or 10% of the paper's values under any reading; the past durations are 368 to 720 ms shorter than the paper's, depending on the reading (368 to 671 ms under epoch reading (a)). Under the claims file's baseline readings (a) and (b), none of the four comparisons reaches p < 0.01 under epoch reading (a) (p from 0.022 to 0.73), nor under epoch reading (b), so the outcome rests on the deposited baseline (assumed).
deviations: The HFA is used as deposited, as the authors' own baseline correction (an assumption): the game epoch is corrected over [-1000, -800] ms (its first window is the same in every trial) and the buttonpress epoch carries a per-trial offset close to it. STAR Methods say only that epochs were made "using a 200-ms baseline to remove any pre-stimulus differences in baseline amplitude", and the data description that "activity for both epochs is temporally aligned". The claims file's readings, (a) the 200 ms before each epoch's event and (b) the 200 ms before game presentation for both epochs (the buttonpress epoch first put on the game epoch's level with its per-trial, per-electrode offset, measured where the epochs overlap), are applied on top of it in the notebook's section Baseline readings.

outcomes.statement: None of the past trial characteristics significantly affected risk taking (all p > 0.15, random effects logistic regression).
outcomes.source: Results, Dissociable OFC Encoding of Past Choice and Outcome Information, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Random effects logistic regression showed that none of the past trial characteristics significantly affected risk-taking
outcomes.notes: Over 1,831 non-timeout rounds with a previous round, with current win probability as a covariate (reading (a)), past risk (beta 1.74, p = 0.015), past chosen value (beta -0.021, p = 0.039) and past RPE (beta 0.017, p = 0.047) are significant at 0.05; the effects are about 0.1 log-odds per SD. Alone (reading (b)), past risk (p = 0.0005) and past chosen value (p = 0.034) are. The paper's all p > 0.15 does not hold under either reading.
deviations: The t-1 regressors are built from all rounds with the authors' convention for a previous timeout (0 for choice and outcome regressors), over all non-timeout rounds, not only those with HFA.

outcomes.statement: Encoding of past information was limited to the immediately preceding trial; the proportion of electrodes encoding choices and outcomes 2 to 5 trials back was significantly lower than for the current and previous trials (p < 0.01, t test), with no evidence of encoding from earlier rounds.
outcomes.source: Results, Dissociable OFC Encoding of Past Choice and Outcome Information, paragraph 3; Figure 6A and 6B
outcomes.quote: Strikingly, we found no evidence for encoding of information from earlier rounds
outcomes.notes: Mean proportions of encoding electrodes over the 8 regressors are 31.8% (t), 34.9% (t-1) and 16.6, 17.7, 16.9 and 19.4% (t-2 to t-5). Reading (a), per-regressor proportions at t-2 to t-5 against t, p = 2.9e-10, and against t-1, p = 7.6e-11; reading (b), the lag means against t, p = 1.9e-04, and against t-1, p = 1.1e-04. No lag from t-2 to t-5 exceeds the 95th percentile of the chance proportion (20.5 to 20.7%, chance mean 18.2 to 18.3%). Only loss index at t-3 exceeds its own 95th percentile. Under the claims file's baseline readings (a) and (b) the outcome is the same (t-2 to t-5 against t and t-1, p from 3.3e-09 to 1.1e-03 under reading (a); no lag above the chance 95th percentile).
deviations: Lags t-2 to t-5 are built from the rounds, as the data set's regressor file holds t-1 only.

outcomes.statement: The distribution of encoding significance at the peak %EV shows a sharp boundary between t-1 and t-2 but not between t and t-1 (one-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests).
outcomes.source: Figure S5C and S5D legends
outcomes.quote: Summary statistical results for ECDFs in (C) highlighting the sharp temporal boundary in encoding extent between t-1 and t-2, but not t and t-1
outcomes.notes: One-sided KS tests on -log10 p at each electrode's peak %EV window (both epochs). t-2 lies above t-1 with p < 0.05 for all 8 regressors (p at most 0.022; pooled D = 0.207, p = 2.6e-29). t-1 lies above t for risk only (p = 0.0002); for the other 7 p = 0.18 to 1 (pooled p = 0.968). 7 of 8 regressors and the pooled test show the boundary between t-1 and t-2 and not between t and t-1. Under the claims file's baseline readings (a) and (b), the pooled t-1 against t test is also significant (p = 3e-05 and 0.0014) and 3 and 4 of 8 regressors show the pattern, so the outcome rests on the deposited baseline (assumed).
deviations: The HFA is used as deposited, as the authors' own baseline correction (an assumption): the game epoch is corrected over [-1000, -800] ms (its first window is the same in every trial) and the buttonpress epoch carries a per-trial offset close to it. STAR Methods say only that epochs were made "using a 200-ms baseline to remove any pre-stimulus differences in baseline amplitude", and the data description that "activity for both epochs is temporally aligned". The claims file's readings, (a) the 200 ms before each epoch's event and (b) the 200 ms before game presentation for both epochs (the buttonpress epoch first put on the game epoch's level with its per-trial, per-electrode offset, measured where the epochs overlap), are applied on top of it in the notebook's section Baseline readings.

outcomes.statement: In nested mixed-effects models with patient and electrode as random effects, all regressors were significant (all p < 10^-4, Bonferroni corrected).
outcomes.source: Results, Dissociable OFC Encoding of Past Choice and Outcome Information, paragraph 4; STAR Methods, Stepwise regression, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: We found that all of our regressors were significantly active
outcomes.notes: All models have patient and electrode within patient as random intercepts (REML), fitted by a closed form in the helper that agrees with statsmodels MixedLM on three fits (slopes and SEs to four or more significant digits, p within 2%). Every combination of the claims file's readings was run. Time point (a), one model per window, Bonferroni over 16 regressors and 114 windows (the game epoch's constant baseline window is skipped): one regressor and all electrodes 14 of 16 reach corrected p < 10^-4, past chosen value (1.7e-03) and past risk (3.0e-03) do not; one regressor and encoding electrodes 11 of 16; all regressors together 11 (all electrodes) and 11 (encoding electrodes) of the 14 that can be estimated, as gamble is the sum of the win and loss indices at t and t-1. Time point (b), HFA averaged over post-event windows, Bonferroni over 16 regressors and 2 epochs: 4, 6, 3 and 3. Under the claims file's baseline reading (a), the per-window model with one regressor and all electrodes makes all 16 significant (largest corrected p 3.3e-05, past gamble), and under (b) 15 (past risk 2.9e-02). The outcome is reproduced, as the criterion passes under one reading; it rests on baseline reading (a) and the per-window reading of the time point (assumed), and is the best of the 24 combinations of readings run. Set after the verifier agreed in round 3. Signed slopes average over electrodes encoding in opposite directions.
deviations: The HFA is used as deposited, as the authors' own baseline correction (an assumption): the game epoch is corrected over [-1000, -800] ms (its first window is the same in every trial) and the buttonpress epoch carries a per-trial offset close to it. STAR Methods say only that epochs were made "using a 200-ms baseline to remove any pre-stimulus differences in baseline amplitude", and the data description that "activity for both epochs is temporally aligned". The claims file's readings, (a) the 200 ms before each epoch's event and (b) the 200 ms before game presentation for both epochs (the buttonpress epoch first put on the game epoch's level with its per-trial, per-electrode offset, measured where the epochs overlap), are applied on top of it in the notebook's section Baseline readings. The outcome rests on baseline reading (a), which the claims file names, with one model per window (assumed).

The nested model is fitted by REML in closed form (helper nested_lmm), which uses the fact that every electrode of a patient shares its trials and regressors; it is checked against statsmodels MixedLM in the notebook. A standard choice.

Time point (b) fits each epoch and counts a regressor when significant in either, with the correction over 16 regressors and 2 epochs. The joint model leaves out the two gamble regressors, which are the sums of the win and loss indices and cannot be estimated with them.

outcomes.statement: Stepwise regression with model selection gave proportions of encoding electrodes per regressor similar to those of the 5-consecutive-window selection.
outcomes.source: Results, Dissociable OFC Encoding of Past Choice and Outcome Information, paragraph 4; Figure S6B
outcomes.quote: The proportion of electrodes encoding each reward-related computational component as estimated by selecting electrodes with ≥5 consecutive encoding windows and stepwise regression followed by model selection were similar
outcomes.notes: After the permutation step (10,000 shuffles, Bonferroni over 191 electrodes) and forward selection, 16 of 191 electrodes keep any regressor; the stepwise proportions are 0 to 2.1% against 20.9 to 49.7% for the 5-window selection. The two are ranked alike (Spearman rho 0.77, p < 0.001, reading (a) holds) but differ by up to 48.2 points (reading (b) fails). The permutation step alone gives 0 to 2.6% (rho 0.65, p = 0.006). On a synthetic electrode the procedure gives p = 0.0005, the smallest possible with 2,000 shuffles. Reading (a) passes only formally, as the stepwise proportions are 0 for 9 of 16 regressors; in substance the two selections are not similar. Under the claims file's baseline readings (a) and (b), stepwise keeps 5 and 4 electrodes, Spearman rho is 0.43 (p = 0.101) and -0.25 (p = 0.349), and the largest difference 42.9 and 38.7 points, so neither reading holds; the outcome also rests on the deposited baseline.
deviations: The HFA is used as deposited, as the authors' own baseline correction (an assumption): the game epoch is corrected over [-1000, -800] ms (its first window is the same in every trial) and the buttonpress epoch carries a per-trial offset close to it. STAR Methods say only that epochs were made "using a 200-ms baseline to remove any pre-stimulus differences in baseline amplitude", and the data description that "activity for both epochs is temporally aligned". The claims file's readings, (a) the 200 ms before each epoch's event and (b) the 200 ms before game presentation for both epochs (the buttonpress epoch first put on the game epoch's level with its per-trial, per-electrode offset, measured where the epochs overlap), are applied on top of it in the notebook's section Baseline readings.

Assumed, as STAR Methods do not say, that the longest significant stretch is taken in each epoch and the larger sum of F used, and that the model comparison (ANOVA) is made on the HFA of the window where the base regressor has its peak %EV. Other readings (a stretch across both epochs, comparisons at each regressor's own peak) were not run; the permutation step, which leaves only 16 electrodes, does not depend on the second choice.
The Bonferroni correction uses the 191 electrodes analysed; the paper says 192.

outcomes.statement: The risk regressor over all trials explains slightly more HFA variance than risk restricted to gamble trials, so risk is encoded whatever the subsequent choice.
outcomes.source: Figure S3A legend
outcomes.quote: The regressor including all trials explains a slightly higher proportion of variance in HFA (%EV), suggesting that risk is encoded regardless of subsequent patient choice
outcomes.notes: Over the 84 risk-encoding electrodes (selected on all trials), the peak mean %EV in the game epoch is 2.32 for all trials and 3.12 for gamble trials only (both at 1,000 ms). Gamble trials are fewer, and the chance peak is also higher for them (2.30 against 1.25), so raw %EV favours the smaller set. With electrodes selected on gamble trials (64), gamble-only gives 3.51 and all trials 1.99. With each chance peak subtracted, all trials come out higher (1.07 against 0.82); the criterion compares raw %EV, so the outcome follows it, but the comparison is confounded by the number of trials. Under the claims file's baseline readings gamble-only is also higher (2.68 against 2.00, 2.88 against 2.54).

outcomes.statement: The direction of the response (left or right option) is not reflected in OFC HFA.
outcomes.source: Figure S3B legend; Results, OFC HFA Reflects Choice- and Outcome-Related Valuation Signals, paragraph 3; Discussion, paragraph beginning "Finally, although ECoG is not affected"
outcomes.quote: Regressors encoding direction of choice (left/right options) are not reflected in OFC HFA
outcomes.notes: 31 electrodes (16.2%) meet the encoding rule for the response side (left = 1), below the shuffled mean (34.7) and the 95th percentile (49); the count is at the 34.5th percentile of the shuffles. The peak mean %EV is 1.61 (game epoch) and 2.00 (buttonpress epoch, at -550 ms), against chance profiles up to 1.25 and 1.26. Under the claims file's baseline readings the count is 35 and 28, below the 95th percentiles 55 and 47.
deviations: The response side is the csv's choice.location.

outcomes.statement: Most electrodes lay in putative Brodmann area 11 (53 of 192), 13 (40) and 14 (67).
outcomes.source: Results, Anatomical Distribution of Present and Past Valuation Signals, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The majority of electrodes in our sample were located in putative BA 11 (n = 53 out of 192 total), 13 (n = 40/192), and 14 (n = 67/192)
outcomes.notes: The data set holds no electrode coordinates, Brodmann labels or anatomy files (the zip members are the HFA mat files and behaviour files only), and the paper names no other deposit.

outcomes.statement: Electrodes encoding each signal type (present and past choice and outcome) were found in all three areas (BA 11, 13 and 14), in similar proportions across areas.
outcomes.source: Results, Anatomical Distribution of Present and Past Valuation Signals, paragraph 1; Figure 7B to 7E; Figure S7A
outcomes.quote: there was strong evidence for the presence of electrodes capturing each type of signal (present and past choice and outcome) across all three areas
outcomes.notes: Needs electrode locations, which are not in the data set (see anatomy-brodmann-counts).

outcomes.statement: There was no consistent evidence for differential encoding of individual valuation components across BA 11, 13 and 14, nor along fronto-posterior or medio-lateral gradients.
outcomes.source: Results, Anatomical Distribution of Present and Past Valuation Signals, paragraph 2; STAR Methods, Anatomical reconstructions; Discussion, paragraph beginning "As electrode locations were based"
outcomes.quote: We found no consistent evidence for differential encoding of individual valuation components across OFC subregions (BA 11/13/14), or across anatomical gradients (fronto-posterior or medio-lateral; STAR Methods)
outcomes.notes: Needs electrode locations and coordinates, which are not in the data set.

outcomes.statement: All signals were present in at least 6 of the 10 patients (mean 7.41 plus or minus 0.4).
outcomes.source: Results, Anatomical Distribution of Present and Past Valuation Signals, paragraph 2; Table S2
outcomes.quote: We found that all signals were present in at least 6 of the 10 patients in our sample (mean = 7.41 ± 0.4; Table S2)
outcomes.notes: Every regressor is present in at least 6 patients (past risk 6, the others 7 to 10). The mean number of patients is 8.62 (SEM 0.27) over the 16 regressors (reading (a)), 8.80 without past risk (b) and 10 over the four groups (c), outside 7.41 plus or minus 0.4 and above the 7.75 Table S2 gives for reading (a). The higher counts follow from the larger numbers of encoding electrodes (fig3-present-encoding). Under the claims file's baseline readings the mean is 8.94 and 8.06 (minimum 8 and 6), also outside the tolerance.
deviations: The HFA is used as deposited; the claims file's baseline readings, shown in the notebook, give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Most electrodes (132 of 192, 68.7%) encoded at least two of the four signal types (choice, outcome, past choice, past outcome) and 30 of 192 (15.6%) encoded all four.
outcomes.source: Results, Anatomical Distribution of Present and Past Valuation Signals, paragraph 3; Figure 7F
outcomes.quote: We observed significant overlap in electrode sets, with most electrodes (n = 132/192; 68.7%) encoding at least two types of signals and 15.6% of electrodes (n = 30/192) encoding all four
outcomes.notes: Under the stepwise selection, 16 electrodes encode one type each (2 choice, 4 past choice, 10 past outcome) and none encodes two or more. Under the 5-window selection (variant) 166 of 191 (86.9%) encode two or more types and 65 (34.0%) all four, both above 132 plus or minus 13.2 and 30 plus or minus 3. Under the claims file's baseline readings the stepwise selection again gives 0 and 0, and the 5-window selection 168 and 63, and 147 and 47.
deviations: The stepwise selection rests on the assumptions of figs6b-stepwise-similar; the outcome does not, as the 5-window selection fails as well.
The HFA is used as deposited; the claims file's baseline readings, shown in the notebook, give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Electrodes encoding both present and t-1 information were overrepresented, for choice (39 of 120, 32.5%, against an expected 31, p < 0.05) and for outcome (43 of 120, 35.8%, against an expected 34, p < 0.01), chi-square tests; many electrodes still encoded only present or only past information.
outcomes.source: Results, Anatomical Distribution of Present and Past Valuation Signals, paragraph 3; Figure S7 legend
outcomes.quote: We found an overrepresentation of electrodes that encoded both t+t-1 regressors both in the case of choice (39/120 or 32.5%, vs. an expected 31/120 or 25.8% under assumption of independence, p<0.05, chi-square test) and outcome information (n=43/120, or 35.8% vs. an expected 34/120 or 28.5% under assumption of independence, p<0.01, chi-square test)
outcomes.notes: Under the stepwise selection (reading (a)) no electrode encodes both present and past information (16 electrodes in all), so the test cannot show overrepresentation. Under the 5-window selection (b) 99 of 184 electrodes encode both present and past choice (99.9 expected, p = 0.73) and 101 both present and past outcome (95.7 expected, p = 0.047). Over all 191 (c) these are 99 (96.2 expected, p = 0.31) and 101 (92.2 expected, p = 0.002). No reading gives counts near 39 and 43 with both overrepresented. Under the claims file's baseline readings the stepwise selection again gives 0 and 0; under the 5-window selection (all encoding electrodes) the counts are 108 and 89, and 98 and 65, none overrepresented at p < 0.05.
deviations: Reading (a) rests on the assumptions of figs6b-stepwise-similar; the outcome does not, as readings (b) and (c) fail as well. The chi-square test is Pearson's without continuity correction, with Yates' correction shown.
The HFA is used as deposited; the claims file's baseline readings, shown in the notebook, give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Example electrodes show risk encoding with an inverted U relation between win probability and HFA at peak encoding, and regret encoding with a linear drop of HFA with regret.
outcomes.source: Figure 2D to 2G legends
outcomes.quote: The relationship follows an inverted u shape with win probabilities as would be expected for risk encoding
outcomes.notes: Of 84 risk-encoding electrodes, 44 have a significant negative quadratic term in win probability at their peak %EV window (an inverted U) and 40 a significant positive one. All 64 regret-encoding electrodes have a significant linear slope on regret at their peak window, 38 with HFA rising with regret (falling as regret becomes more negative) and 26 the other way. The regret half holds by construction, as an electrode selected for encoding regret has a significant slope at its peak window. Under the claims file's baseline readings 32 of 75 and 18 of 66 risk electrodes show an inverted U and all regret electrodes a slope.

findings.statement: The data description says 192 electrodes are in the data set; the files hold 199. In s03, electrodes 52 to 58 are exact copies of electrodes 45 to 51 in both the 1-kHz and the window arrays (deposited twice). Without them the per-patient counts match Table S2.

In s03, electrode 42's 1-kHz arrays are copies of electrode 34's, and its window arrays are copies of electrode 41's, so its window averages do not come from its own 1-kHz data and neither array holds data of its own. Every other electrode's windows equal the mean of samples 50k to 50k+200 of its 1-kHz data.

The buttonpress epochs are described as centred on the button press. Per subject they are centred a fixed 470 to 600 ms after the csv's buttonpress.time (measured from choice.time), and the gamble outcome is encoded from about 200 ms after their time 0 and not in the game epoch. This fits epochs locked to the outcome reveal, as the paper's Figure 3C labels them; it is consistent with the data, not shown, as the true event times are not in the files.
The csv column reveal.time is 0.53 to 0.59 s after buttonpress.time in s01 to s05, near the 550 ms the description and the paper give, but 0.03 to 0.05 s in s06 to s10 (up to 0.24 s in s10).

The HFA trials carry no round number. They are fewer than the non-timeout rounds in 8 of 10 subjects (1,753 against 1,839). They can be matched to rounds only through the regressor values in sXX_behav_globals.mat, which match every trial here.
86 non-timeout rounds (2 to 19 per subject, none in s08 and s09) have no HFA trial; the description does not say why (the paper mentions excluding epochs with aberrant activity).

The description says each patient played 200 rounds with a 2-s limit and that timeouts were 9.98% of trials. s10 has 138 rounds, no timeouts and reaction times with a median of 4.4 s and a maximum of 80.5 s; s06 to s09 have 102 reaction times above 2 s (up to 2.5 s); timeouts are 99 of 1,938 rounds (5.1%).

The csv column choice.time is not described (it is 0.66 to 0.97 s after trial start, read here as game presentation). The units of the HFA values are not stated, nor that the game epochs are baseline-corrected (their first 200-ms window is constant across trials in every electrode). The buttonpress epochs differ from the game epochs, where they overlap, by a per-trial constant of -4.86 to 3.28 on the first electrode (medians per subject -3.26 to 0.83, over 1,572 of 1,753 trials where the epochs overlap; trial-level SD 5.2), so they carry an undocumented per-trial offset close to the game epoch's correction.

In s07 to s10 the chosen side agrees with gamble_choices.csv's Risky.Side in only 87 to 97.5% of rounds (in every round for s01 to s06), although the outcomes agree with the csv's shown and hidden numbers in every round. The gamble prizes in gamble_choices.csv are $15 to $30, where the description says $10 to $30.
The data set holds no broadband signal, no electrode coordinates or Brodmann labels, and no data from the 10 healthy participants. Six of the paper's findings cannot be tested.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook of the first run with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier tested encoding_scan, longest_run, run_bounds and glmm_logit on synthetic inputs and read the zip directories of the archive by range requests. Its outcomes agree with the record for all 28 claims; it marked mixed-effects-robust provisional. In reply, the revision ran both of the claims file's baseline readings over every test that rests on the encoding scans (a new notebook section), ran every combination of the mixed-effects readings with the nested model, printed the variables of the HFA files and the mean offset between the epochs, checked the trial matching in reverse, added the criterion's non-timeout variant for the regressor R2, and added point 10 to questions/saez-2018.yaml for a reader. No outcome changed; four more outcomes (fig4-past-encoding, fig5-past-sustained, figs5d-sharp-boundary and mixed-effects-robust) are now marked as resting on the deposited baseline, on which figs6b-stepwise-similar also rests. Report in transcripts/saez-2018/verifier-1-report.md.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the revision after round 1, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file, the README and this record, with the paper. The verifier agrees with 27 of the 28 outcomes and disagrees with mixed-effects-robust, which it would give as reproduced (assumed) under the claims file's baseline reading (a). It also found that baseline reading (b) was not cleanly applied to the buttonpress epoch, which carries its own per-trial offset. In reply, the revision keeps every verified outcome and proposes reproduced for mixed-effects-robust under proposed; it measures the buttonpress epoch's per-trial, per-electrode offset on every trial where the two epochs overlap (1,572 of 1,753 trials; the electrode's median elsewhere) and re-runs baseline reading (b) with it, which changes no outcome; it prints reveal.time per subject (the finding is corrected), the pair behind the averaged maximum R2, and the largest corrected p of the mixed models under each baseline; it corrects the sentences the report quotes; it removes the assumed flag from fig7f-multiplexing and figs7-present-past-overlap; and it adds the verifier's round-1 point 3 to questions/saez-2018.yaml for a reader. Report in transcripts/saez-2018/verifier-2-report.md.

disagreements.reason: The claims file says it is reproduced when, under one reading, every regressor has corrected p < 10^-4, and lists baseline (a) as an allowed reading. Under baseline (a), one model per window with one regressor and all electrodes makes all 16 significant. The implementation of baseline (a) is exact, as subtracting the window centred at -100 ms removes any constant per-trial offset. The record treats the deposited baseline as the only primary analysis; for this claim that blocks a pass a claims-file reading gives. The outcome should be reproduced, with assumed true, resting on baseline reading (a) and the per-window Bonferroni reading. The text says the fit "matches statsmodels MixedLM to the printed digits"; cell 85 shows small differences.

verifications.reviewed: Round 3. Only the change of outcome proposed after round 2, for mixed-effects-robust, with the executed notebook, the helper module, the claims file and the paper. Report in transcripts/saez-2018/verifier-3-report.md.

paper_notes.statement: The encoding rule as the Methods give it (p < 0.05 in 5 or more consecutive 200-ms windows stepped by 50 ms, anywhere in either 3-s epoch) classifies 18.2% of electrodes as encoding when the labels are shuffled, more than Table S2 reports for chosen value and past risk. How do the 1,000 shuffles enter the selection? Requiring each electrode to beat its own shuffled null gives counts all below Table S2; the plain rule gives counts above it. Were the windows limited to part of the epochs, or the p-values taken from the shuffles?

For the stepwise regression, is the longest significant stretch taken within each epoch or across both, and on which HFA (which window or average) are the nested models compared by ANOVA? With a Bonferroni correction over 192 electrodes and 10,000 shuffles, 16 of 191 electrodes keep any regressor here.

For the nested mixed-effects models, what is the dependent variable in time (each window or an average), are the regressors entered alone or together (gamble is the sum of the win and loss indices, so all 16 cannot be estimated together), are random slopes included, and over what is the Bonferroni correction made? With fixed slopes over electrodes that encode in opposite directions, the result depends strongly on these choices and on the baseline here (3 to 14 of 16 regressors at corrected p < 10^-4 with the deposited HFA, 16 of 16 per window after subtracting each epoch's own 200-ms pre-event baseline).

The delays and durations of choice and outcome encoding (512.5 and 287 ms; 612.15 and 712.5 ms) are not defined. Are they per regressor, from the mean %EV profile or the share of encoding electrodes, and is the buttonpress epoch locked to the button press or to the outcome reveal?

STAR Methods say epochs were made using a 200-ms baseline but not which 200 ms or how it was removed. The deposited game epochs are already corrected over [-1000, -800] ms around game presentation, before the fixation cross. Is that the correction the published analyses used, and was the buttonpress epoch corrected with the same window? Subtracting each epoch's own 200 ms before its event changes the outcomes of five claims here (fig4-past-encoding, fig5-past-sustained, figs5d-sharp-boundary, figs6b-stepwise-similar and mixed-effects-robust).

entries.name: saez-2018
entries.title: Reward-related HFA encoding in human OFC (Saez et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Saez, Lin, Stolk, Chang, Parvizi, Schalk, Knight and Hsu (2018) on CRCNS ofc-3, which holds orbitofrontal high-frequency activity epochs and behaviour of 10 epilepsy patients playing a gambling task. It tests the behaviour, the regression of HFA on choice, outcome and past-trial regressors, the timing and duration of encoding, the stepwise and mixed-effects checks and the overlap of electrode sets. The broadband signal, the electrode locations and the healthy participants' data are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Saez et al. (2018) from CRCNS ofc-3
